features.name: credits_others_for_own_success
features.question: Does the author credit specific other people for helping them reach an achievement of their own?
features.definition: The author names or describes people who helped them succeed and attributes part of the success to them.
features.yes_example: I would never have finished this degree without my mentor Sara.
features.no_example: I finished my degree this week.
features.hypothesis: Gratitude aimed at helpers may be what drives the thanks effect.

features.name: spotlights_one_person
features.question: Is most of the post about one specific person other than the author?
features.definition: A single named or described individual, not the author, is the main subject of most of the post.
features.yes_example: Meet Lina, our first engineer, who rebuilt our platform in a month.
features.no_example: Our engineering team rebuilt the platform in a month.
features.hypothesis: Single-person spotlights narrow the story-about-individual effect.

features.name: education_milestone
features.question: Does the post announce that the author completed a degree, course, or certification?
features.definition: The author reports finishing an educational program or earning a credential.
features.yes_example: Officially a certified project manager as of today.
features.no_example: Here are five courses worth taking this year.
features.hypothesis: Credential news may collect congratulations like career news.

features.name: describes_turning_point
features.question: Does the post describe a specific decision or moment that changed the direction of the author's life or career?
features.definition: The author identifies one moment or choice as a turning point in their path.
features.yes_example: The day I turned down that offer changed everything.
features.no_example: Careers rarely follow a straight line.
features.hypothesis: Turning points are a sharper form of personal story.

features.name: ends_with_takeaway_sentence
features.question: Does the post end with a one-sentence general lesson or takeaway?
features.definition: The final sentence states a general lesson drawn from what came before.
features.yes_example: ...Lesson: the best hires are often the ones you almost passed on.
features.no_example: ...See you all at the next meetup!
features.hypothesis: Common hook-and-lesson advice; test the ending.

features.name: live_update_today
features.question: Does the post describe something happening to the author today or right now?
features.definition: The post reports an event the author is experiencing on the day of posting, in the present.
features.yes_example: Today I'm on stage at the Lisbon summit, talking about climate data.
features.no_example: Last year I spoke at a summit in Lisbon.
features.hypothesis: Live, in-the-moment updates may feel more personal.

features.name: self_deprecating_humor
features.question: Does the author make a joke at their own expense?
features.definition: The author uses humor that pokes fun at themselves, their skills, or their situation.
features.yes_example: My code worked on the first try, so naturally I assumed something was broken.
features.no_example: Our code passed every test on the first try.
features.hypothesis: Narrower than general humor, which had no effect.

features.name: looks_forward_with_excitement
features.question: Does the author say they are excited or looking forward to something coming next?
features.definition: The author states excitement or anticipation about a future step, event, or chapter.
features.yes_example: Can't wait to start this next chapter in Berlin.
features.no_example: This chapter in Berlin is over.
features.hypothesis: Forward-looking excitement is typical of announcements; test it alone.

features.name: learned_from_a_person
features.question: Does the post describe something the author learned from a specific person?
features.definition: The author attributes a lesson or insight to an interaction with a particular individual.
features.yes_example: My first manager taught me to always write the agenda first.
features.no_example: Always write the agenda first.
features.hypothesis: Lessons attached to people may avoid the generic-advice penalty.

features.name: asks_readers_to_share_their_story
features.question: Does the post ask readers to share a personal experience of their own?
features.definition: Readers are invited to describe something that happened to them.
features.yes_example: What was the moment you knew you were in the right job?
features.no_example: What do you think of the new policy?
features.hypothesis: Experience questions may work better than opinion questions, which hurt.

features.name: uses_exclusive_event
features.question: Does the post explicitly state that attendance at an event is limited, by invitation only, or subject to approval/RSVP?
features.definition: The post indicates that not everyone can attend; access is restricted by capacity, invitation, or screening.
features.yes_example: A limited number of invitations remain; attendance is by approved RSVP only.
features.no_example: Everyone is welcome to join our open meetup on Friday.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to predict higher reactions because scarcity and exclusivity increase perceived value and FOMO.

features.name: enumerates_root_causes
features.question: Does the post present one ambiguous observation (such as a customer complaint) and then list at least three distinct possible underlying causes?
features.definition: The post takes a single symptom or statement and breaks it into multiple potential explanations.
features.yes_example: Customer says 'I don't understand.' It could be a product, messaging, or trust problem.
features.no_example: The product failed because the UI was confusing.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to predict higher reactions because diagnostic frameworks are perceived as insightful and useful.

features.name: reports_external_accreditation
features.question: Does the post report that an external organization (not the author's own) achieved a specific accreditation, certification, or recognized standard?
features.definition: The post states that a third-party entity received formal recognition, credential, or accreditation.
features.yes_example: PECB became the first certification body with UKAS accreditation for ISO 42001.
features.no_example: Our company recently obtained ISO certification.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to predict higher reactions because third-party validation lends authority and news value.

features.name: curates_resources_with_descriptions
features.question: Does the post list at least three external resources (links, tools, courses) and provide a short description of each resource's purpose?
features.definition: The post offers multiple resources, each accompanied by a one-sentence explanation of what it is for.
features.yes_example: Remote Rocketship – free resource for remote talent; Remotive – curated remote tech jobs.
features.no_example: Here are links: link1, link2, link3.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to predict higher reactions because annotated lists save time and increase usefulness.

features.name: invites_speaker_submission
features.question: Does the post invite readers to submit a proposal, talk, or application to speak or present at an event, rather than just attend?
features.definition: The post includes a call for speakers or presenters, asking readers to apply to give a talk.
features.yes_example: Azure Tour Tenerife has an open call for speakers. Send your proposal by October 24.
features.no_example: Tickets are on sale for the conference.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to predict higher reactions because calls for speakers engage a niche professional audience who share with peers.

features.name: celebrates_local_pride
features.question: Does the post celebrate a local community, city, or regional identity (e.g., a city's day, a local song, a hometown reference) as a point of pride?
features.definition: The post expresses affection or pride for a specific place or local culture, often on a commemorative day.
features.yes_example: Happy 901 Day, Memphis! No place like the M.
features.no_example: We opened a new office in Memphis last month.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to predict higher reactions because local pride triggers emotional resonance and sharing within a community.

features.name: contrasts_related_metrics
features.question: Does the post present two or more related statistics or metrics and explicitly note that together they reveal a non-obvious insight?
features.definition: The post juxtaposes quantitative data points that seem contradictory or surprising when combined.
features.yes_example: Deal volume fell 8%, but the median multiple hit a record 18.8x; together they signal a flight to quality.
features.no_example: Deal volume fell 8% last quarter.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to predict lower reactions because abstract statistical contrasts without immediate actionable advice can feel less engaging.

features.name: states_short_time_to_value
features.question: Does the post state a specific short time frame (e.g., 'days', 'hours', 'instantly') for a product or service to deliver value or be implemented?
features.definition: The post quantifies how quickly the reader can see results or get set up using a product.
features.yes_example: Connects to your AEM setup and helps most teams go live within days.
features.no_example: Our product is powerful and secure.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to predict higher reactions because concrete time-to-value reduces perceived risk.

features.name: parallel_question_sequence
features.question: Does the post ask at least three questions in a row that begin with the same word or share a repeated grammatical structure?
features.definition: Three or more consecutive interrogative sentences use an identical opening word or parallel syntax.
features.yes_example: What is your goal? What is your plan? What is your deadline?
features.no_example: What is your goal? Then think about your plan and deadline.
features.hypothesis: I expect parallel question sequences to do better; they create rhythm and prompt multiple reflections.

features.name: asks_readers_to_reply_with_number_or_keyword_from_list
features.question: Does the post ask the reader to reply with a specific number, keyword, or short phrase that corresponds to an item or option listed in the post?
features.definition: The post contains a question or directive that asks the reader to select from options presented in the post and respond with the chosen number, letter, emoji, or keyword.
features.yes_example: Which of these three mistakes have you made? Reply 1, 2, or 3.
features.no_example: Let me know your thoughts in the comments.
features.hypothesis: Posts that ask readers to select from a presented list reduce response effort and increase interactions.

features.name: states_number_of_items_before_list
features.question: Does the post explicitly state the total number of items (e.g., 'three reasons', 'five steps') before presenting a list or sequence?
features.definition: The post includes a phrase that announces the number of points, components, steps, or reasons that will follow, before those items are enumerated.
features.yes_example: Here are four ways to improve your onboarding.
features.no_example: Let's look at ways to improve onboarding.
features.hypothesis: Announcing a specific count before a list gives readers a clear roadmap, making the post feel more structured.

features.name: asks_reader_to_tag_someone
features.question: Does the post explicitly ask readers to tag, mention, or share the post with another specific person in the comments?
features.definition: The post includes a directive that asks the reader to tag a colleague, friend, or specific account in the comments, often using the phrase 'tag someone who' or 'tag them below'.
features.yes_example: Tag a colleague who needs to hear this.
features.no_example: Share your thoughts below.
features.hypothesis: Tag requests encourage readers to involve their network, increasing distribution and reactions.

features.name: opens_with_contradiction
features.question: Does the post open with a sentence or pair of sentences that presents a direct contradiction or tension between two concepts, without immediately resolving it?
features.definition: The first line of the post juxtaposes two incompatible statements, expectations, or claims, often using the structure 'X says Y, but Z' or 'X is not Y; it is Z'.
features.yes_example: Your CRM says leads are up, but revenue is down.
features.no_example: Here are some tips for improving your CRM.
features.hypothesis: Leading with an unresolved contradiction hooks readers by creating curiosity.

features.name: bilingual_content
features.question: Does the post include at least one complete sentence written in a second language alongside the primary language?
features.definition: The post contains parallel or translated content in two different languages, with at least one full sentence in each language.
features.yes_example: Looking for my next role. מחפש את הצעד הבא בקריירה.
features.no_example: Looking for my next role in marketing leadership.
features.hypothesis: I expect bilingual posts to do better than expected; they can broaden audience and feel inclusive.

features.name: letter_style_opening
features.question: Does the post open with a salutation addressed to a specific role, company type, or audience segment?
features.definition: The first words are a direct address such as 'Dear [specific group]' or 'To [role/type]', treating the post like a letter.
features.yes_example: Dear Series C SaaS founders scaling into Europe:
features.no_example: If you're a Series C founder scaling into Europe, this matters.
features.hypothesis: I expect this letter-style opening to do better; it targets readers precisely.

features.name: controversy_allegation_named_company
features.question: Does the post describe a specific allegation, controversy, or ethical dispute involving a named company or its technology?
features.definition: The post reports an accusation or disputed action tied to a named organization, not just a general industry issue.
features.yes_example: OpenAI allegedly used researchers' notes without permission.
features.no_example: OpenAI released a new model today.
features.hypothesis: I expect posts about a named company controversy to do better; controversy drives attention and discussion.

features.name: mentions_time_of_day
features.question: Does the post mention a specific time of day, such as '3am', 'morning', or 'midnight'?
features.definition: The post includes a clock time or period of the day, making the narrative more concrete.
features.yes_example: I woke at 5am to work.
features.no_example: I woke early to work.
features.hypothesis: Including a specific time of day adds concreteness and personal detail, potentially increasing engagement.

features.name: uses_curiosity_gap_opening
features.question: Does the post open by hinting at surprising or important information without revealing it immediately?
features.definition: The first sentence or two promise an insight or fact but delay stating what it is, forcing the reader to continue for the answer.
features.yes_example: Most people miss one thing about pricing, and it costs them.
features.no_example: Here are three pricing tips: test, anchor, and bundle.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to increase reactions because curiosity gaps drive reading.

features.name: describes_unexpected_result_from_test
features.question: Does the post narrate an experiment, test, or trial that produced an unexpected or unintended outcome?
features.definition: The post tells a short story about a deliberate test or trial that went differently than planned, often with humorous or surprising consequences.
features.yes_example: We gave an AI a budget and it bought 500 coffee bags.
features.no_example: We tested our AI, and it worked as expected.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to increase reactions because unexpected outcomes are shareable and memorable.

features.name: highlights_free_help_or_charity
features.question: Does the post highlight a person or group giving free help, education, or charity to others without promoting a paid product?
features.definition: The post focuses on someone else's unpaid assistance, free teaching, or charitable act, not on a commercial offering by the author.
features.yes_example: This teacher gives free coding classes to 100 kids every weekend.
features.no_example: We offer affordable coding bootcamps starting at $99.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to increase reactions because inspirational altruism resonates emotionally.

features.name: asks_reader_to_self_identify_from_options
features.question: Does the post present a set of options or categories and ask the reader to indicate which one applies to them?
features.definition: The post lists at least two distinct groups, roles, or choices and directly invites the reader to say which one describes them or their situation.
features.yes_example: Which founder type are you: builder, seller, or operator? Comment below.
features.no_example: Here are three founder types you should know.
features.hypothesis: I expect this to increase reactions because it invites personal participation.

features.name: multiple_choice_question_end
features.question: Does the post end with a question that presents two or more specific options for the reader to choose between?
features.definition: Answer yes if the final sentence is a question offering a closed set of choices, such as 'X or Y?' or 'A, B, or C?'
features.yes_example: Would you add security or cost first?
features.no_example: What do you think about this?
features.hypothesis: Ending with a multiple-choice question is expected to do better; it provides a low-friction response prompt.
